question: Who wins new federal awards each year: how many companies, how many are new, how many stay, how concentrated the dollars are, and how new companies relate to single-offer awards.
headline_series: awards above $25,000 (initial potential value; dollars not adjusted for inflation)

definitions.company: one company id: vendor_id, with DUNS-based and UEI-based codes linked into one id wherever a record carries both
definitions.new_company: won no award in the 3 previous fiscal years (in the above-$25,000 series: no award above $25,000)
definitions.new_company_never_seen: won no award in any earlier year present (since FY2008)
definitions.staying: won again in the next fiscal year, or within the next three fiscal years
definitions.top_shares: share of initial dollars won by the top 1% and top 10% of companies, ranked by initial dollars
definitions.hhi: Herfindahl-Hirschman index of initial dollars within a 4-digit NAICS industry with at least 20 awards in the year (sum of squared percentage shares, 0 to 10,000); summarized as the award-weighted median and the share of awards in industries above 2,500

usaspending_sample.what: Do contract records from before the April 2022 switch carry a UEI on USAspending.gov today? One small sample, checked once.
usaspending_sample.source: USAspending.gov download service, POST https://api.usaspending.gov/api/v2/download/transactions/ (no key or account)
usaspending_sample.reading: Every sampled FY2010 transaction carries a UEI, so USAspending has filled in UEIs on old records; a company's vendor_id is UEI-based before and after the switch whenever its records got a UEI. One agency and five days only: a check, not a measurement.

companies_all_awards.note_first_year: FY2008 reporting change: Department of Veterans Affairs reported 806,913 purchase orders, 741,240 of them at or under $3,000 (FY2009: 82,164 and 4,360); counts of all awards are not comparable with later years; use the above-$25,000 series

notes_in_tables: FY2008 reporting change: Department of Veterans Affairs reported 806,913 purchase orders, 741,240 of them at or under $3,000 (FY2009: 82,164 and 4,360); counts of all awards are not comparable with later years; use the above-$25,000 series
new-company measures not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2019, FY2020, FY2021 cannot link the two yet
new-company measures not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2020, FY2021 cannot link the two yet
new-company measures not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2021 cannot link the two yet
new-company measures: the look-back includes the FY2008 reporting change of Department of Veterans Affairs; use the above-$25,000 series

next-year staying not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2021 cannot link the two yet; three-year staying not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2021 cannot link the two yet
three-year staying not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2019, FY2020, FY2021 cannot link the two yet
three-year staying not comparable: company identifiers changed from DUNS to UEI in April 2022, and the tables of FY2020, FY2021 cannot link the two yet
caveats: A company is one identifier. A company can hold several identifiers (one per registered entity), and parents and subsidiaries count as different companies, so the counts are counts of registered entities, not of corporate families.
Only prime awards: subcontractors are not counted.
Only new awards (base actions): orders placed under existing contract vehicles (delivery and task orders) are not in these tables, so a company that wins only such orders does not appear.

Dollars are the initial potential value (base and all options) of purchase orders and definitive contracts, not adjusted for inflation; negative values count as zero. Contract vehicles are left out of dollar measures because their value is a ceiling, and values above $10 billion are left out as likely recording errors.

Counts of all awards depend on how very small purchases were reported, which changed over time (for example the FY2008 Veterans Affairs micro-purchases and the higher micro-purchase limits from FY2016 and FY2018); the series of awards above $25,000 is the headline for that reason.
Until April 2022 companies were identified by DUNS numbers, after that by UEI. The tables link the two where a record carries both; rows marked 'not comparable' could not be checked.
The latest Defense year is incomplete until its last quarter is published, 90 days late.
These are patterns in public data, not accusations and not proof of causes.
privacy: No company or buying office is named or coded in any output; no statistic describes a single company; cells resting on fewer than 10 companies are blank.
